contexts.description: Visual ability-spec blueprint editor: wiring graph, tag-rules editor, effect timeline editor, loadout editor, relationship web, template picker with presets, and a real-time simulation sandbox (queue, graphs, sparklines). Generates structured UE5 blueprint spec code from a GUI, closing the loop between visual design and engine output.
contexts.name: ability-blueprint

contexts.description: Full-stack ability and GAS (Gameplay Ability System) design suite: authors ability specs, computes balance formulas, generates GAS C++ code, and validates tags. The forge sub-system lets designers tune attribute weights interactively. Cross-references the character blueprint to keep ability tags in sync with the UE5 project.
contexts.name: ability-design

contexts.description: AI-assisted ability forge: a prompt-driven ability generation panel with diff viewer (code diff + ability diff), adopt bar, refine bar, forge history, prompt inspector, stat bar, and tag row. Designers describe an ability in natural language and receive structured UE5-ready code with a one-click adopt flow. Integrates with the CLI task system via the forge adopt hook.
contexts.name: ability-forge

contexts.description: Gameplay Ability System (GAS) balance tooling and attribute/tag management: level-sweep simulation, sensitivity charts, histogram, results analysis, scenario editor, import modal, and balance health report. Tag section provides attribute growth charts, relationship web, tag audit, tag dependency view, and quick-view popover. These tools validate GAS attribute balance across levels before generating UE5 code.
contexts.name: ability-gas-balance

contexts.description: Core ARPG ability spellbook: command palette search, ability listing with cooldown wheels, compare radar, damage-calc section, loadout section, effects timeline, and shared ability data/types. Also houses the module root, spellbook search index, feature metrics, and the narrative breadcrumb. This is the designer's primary entry point for authoring and browsing abilities.
contexts.name: ability-spellbook-core

contexts.description: Provides authoring and testing tools for enemy AI behavior: cover-usage analysis, flank-angle heatmaps, and a scenario sandbox where designers run fresh test suites against AI logic. Data flows from user-edited scenario configs through useAITesting/useModuleCLI hooks to Claude CLI prompts, with results surfaced in visual overlays. Depends on the module-registry prompt system and projectStore for UE5 path context.
contexts.name: ai-behavior-testing

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/claude-terminal/stream, GET /api/claude-terminal/query, POST /api/one-shot/analyze, POST /api/one-shot/propose, POST /api/one-shot/refine, POST /api/one-shot/step, GET /api/one-shot/status/[executionId], POST /api/agents/forge-ability, GET /api/agents/live-token, GET/POST /api/model-policy, GET/POST /api/model-benchmarks
contexts.description: Hosts the AI-powered developer acceleration APIs: Claude terminal streaming, one-shot code execution pipeline (analyze → propose → refine → step → status), agent endpoints for ability forging and live token tracking, prompt evolution, codebase archaeology, asset-code oracle, model policy/benchmarks management, AI testing harness, and structured insights extraction. Acts as the backbone of the app's AI-assisted development loop.
contexts.name: ai-developer-tools-api

contexts.description: Animation video generation pipeline using Leonardo Hailuo for text-to-video and image-to-video. The anim-critique module applies a VLM aesthetic ruler to multi-frame filmstrips scoring six dimensions (anticipation, weight, timing, follow-through, silhouette, believability) and returning a topFix suggestion. This closes the loop on animation quality without human review for every iteration.
contexts.name: anim-video-gen

contexts.description: Drives AI-assisted combat combo choreography and animation import tooling. The AIComboChoreographer parses natural-language combo descriptions into montage timelines and combo chain graphs with root-motion preview, while AnimationChecklist tracks the per-step animation production checklist and MixamoImport manages clip import from Mixamo. These tools bridge design intent to UE5 montage and animation asset production.
contexts.name: animation-combo-workflow

contexts.description: Animation combo and montage editing plus the metrics dashboard: combo chain graph SVG, combo/event timeline panels, frame scrubber, safe-montage hook, and a full suite of metrics (assets, chains, heatmap, montages, play-rate, scrubber, skeleton, states, trajectories, transitions). Lets designers audit montage coverage and combo correctness against the animation budget.
contexts.name: animation-combos-metrics

contexts.description: Animation pipeline tools covering retargeting from Mixamo/MHA sources to UE5 Manny, state graph authoring, combo/montage sequencing, and runtime budget tracking. The anim-critique tier applies a VLM aesthetic ruler to multi-frame filmstrips scoring anticipation, weight, timing, follow-through, silhouette, and believability. Integrates with the harness for closed-loop code-authored animation via numeric FK feedback.
contexts.name: animation-module

contexts.description: Animation state-machine and budget tooling: a live SVG state-machine graph with state-group browser and responsiveness analyzer, blend-space panel, state-duration panel, montage asset browser, animation reality ledger, and budget coverage panels. Gives designers a read on animation state complexity and blend-space health before shipping to UE5.
contexts.name: animation-state-graph

contexts.description: A full interactive editor for authoring UE5 animation state machines — drag-and-drop canvas, state and transition property panels, live warnings, and C++ Blueprint code generation. It maintains a draft Zustand store for in-progress edits and a codegen module that emits compilable UE5 C++ or Blueprint text. Exports to Blender NLA strips and previews generated output in a syntax-highlighted code panel.
contexts.name: animation-state-machine-editor

contexts.description: Provides a read-only visual diagram of a UE5 AnimBlueprint state machine — nodes, edges, and per-state detail panels — sourced from a live AnimBP scan. It parses the scanned graph into React Flow nodes and edges, renders them with custom node/edge components, and exposes detail panels for transitions and states. Depends on the shared state-machine type definitions and the StateMachineEditor context for authoring.
contexts.name: animation-state-machine-viewer

contexts.description: Next.js App Router shell with tab-based navigation between module domains. The LRU module cache suspends hidden modules to pause their timers and subscriptions. useSuspendableEffect and useSuspendableSelector are the standard hooks for suspension-aware work. The app shell tracks hydration state to gate portals and document access, preventing SSR/client mismatches.
contexts.name: app-navigation

contexts.description: Provides the outer application frame: the two-tier sidebar (L1 module picker, L2 feature navigator with progress rings and status badges), CLI terminal panels (tab bar + bottom drawer), module-level error boundaries, and loading skeletons. AppShell wires the layout together while ModuleRenderer resolves the active module from the registry and mounts it, with SidebarL2 tracking per-module checklist progress from Zustand.
contexts.name: app-shell-and-chrome

contexts.description: AI-powered asset generation studio that turns text prompts and style DNA into 2D images, 3D meshes, and cloth simulations. Users build prompts through a guided PromptBuilder, submit generation jobs, and receive critiqued results that feed into a queue. Depends on the visual-gen provider APIs and pof-mcp generation tools; outputs feed the asset-viewer and UE5 import pipeline.
contexts.name: asset-forge

contexts.api_surface: Reads /api/assets/* for library contents; calls pof-mcp asset_library tool
contexts.description: Combined 3D asset viewport and local asset library. The viewer renders GLB/FBX assets with a SceneViewer, computes quality grades (assetGrade) and render stats, and exposes viewport status overlays and a toolbar. The browser side provides collection-organised library browsing with LibraryPanel, BrowsePanel, and dual Zustand stores (useAssetBrowserStore, useAssetLibraryStore). Together they let artists inspect generated outputs and curate a reusable asset collection.
contexts.name: asset-viewer-and-browser

contexts.description: Provides tooling to scout, acquire, and visually tune game assets: AssetScoutView recommends and tracks acquired assets with integration status rows; PostProcessStudioView is a full post-process parameter studio with effect cards, GPU cost breakdown, preset gallery, and before/after compare bars. Together they bridge asset discovery through visual polish to UE5-ready configuration. AssetScoutView reads from the asset_library table; PostProcessStudioView targets the post_process_presets table.
contexts.name: asset-visual-studio

contexts.description: Covers audio code generation, spatial audio room analysis, library management, and supporting display utilities for the audio module. SpatialAudioGeneratorPanel generates UE5 C++ spatial audio configurations from room descriptions; SoundForgePanel and AudioCodeGenPanel drive CLI-backed code generation prompts; AudioLibraryPanel and AudioPipelineDiagram visualize the audio asset pipeline. Shared display components (WaveformThumbnail, ReverbDecayGlyph, LicenseBadge, AudioUsageMeter) are consumed across the audio module.
contexts.name: audio-generation-tools

contexts.description: Audio scene management, asset library, and AI voice/SFX/music generation. Supports spatial audio design with scene-viewport tools, voice activity detection, and ElevenLabs integration via a provider mesh. Assets are persisted with content-hash deduplication and can be wired to Unreal audio events.
contexts.name: audio-module

contexts.description: Provides a spatial audio scene painting canvas and an emitter/zone property editing panel. The AudioScenePainter lets designers place sound emitters and zones on a 2D canvas with draw, zoom, and minimap tools, persisting emitter positions and zone boundaries. AudioPropertyPanel exposes editable properties for selected emitters and zones including asset-set selection, reverb, and attenuation parameters with debounced commit to the database.
contexts.name: audio-scene-designer

contexts.description: The main AudioView shell with tab navigation (Painter, Soundscapes, Settings) plus the AudioEventCatalog for browsing and editing named audio events grouped by category. AudioView composes the scene painter tab with a sidebar showing zone/scene context, while AudioEventCatalog lets designers create, edit, and delete event entries stored in the audioEventCatalogStore (Zustand). These two surfaces together cover the full audio-design authoring session.
contexts.name: audio-view-and-catalog

contexts.description: Enemy archetype library and AI-logic designer: archetype builder, grid, cards, filters, expanded details, radar comparison, prestige lifecycle panel, codegen modal, and behavior-tree flowchart with decision debugger, perception cone visualization, aggro table. Lets designers author enemy types and their decision trees visually, then generate UE5 BehaviorTree assets.
contexts.name: bestiary-archetypes-ai

contexts.description: Encounter design and bestiary analytics: difficulty charts, spawn formation visualizer, tactics map, kill/death stats, encounter sub-parts, and a full metrics suite (aggro, behavior-tree, cards, decision log, difficulty, formations, modifiers, radar, waves). Used to validate encounter balance and spawn formation logic before committing to the catalog.
contexts.name: bestiary-encounters-metrics

contexts.description: Blender MCP (Model Context Protocol) integration enabling direct Blender scripting from the app via a TCP bridge. Supports mesh generation, material application, and pipeline export to UE5 formats. The 3D studio components provide an in-browser WebGL/Three.js preview of generated assets. Guided setup walks users through the Blender connection.
contexts.name: blender-3d-integration

contexts.api_surface: Internal singleton: getService() → BlenderMCPService (connect, probe, executeCode, getSceneInfo, getViewportScreenshot, searchPolyHaven, downloadPolyHaven, searchSketchfab, downloadSketchfab, generateHyper3D, generateHunyuan3D, pollJobStatus, importGeneratedAsset)
contexts.description: Provides a TCP bridge from the PoF app to a locally-running Blender instance via the ahujasid/blender-mcp addon. The service singleton serializes all commands on a single socket (no request-id wire protocol), enforces per-class timeouts and an 8 MB receive-buffer cap, and exposes typed helpers for scene queries, Python script execution, viewport screenshots, PolyHaven/Sketchfab asset sourcing, and 3D generation jobs (Hyper3D / Hunyuan3D). Script modules under scripts/ generate ready-to-execute Blender Python for tasks like armature creation, IK setup, LOD generation, NLA state machines, terrain/dungeon mesh conversion, UV projection, compositor stacks, and FBX export.
contexts.name: blender-mcp-bridge

contexts.api_surface: Calls Blender MCP server via TCP; produces FBX files consumed by UE5 import
contexts.description: Blender-backed mesh processing pipeline that runs LOD generation, mesh optimisation, and FBX conversion via a local Blender TCP/MCP bridge. Users write or select Python scripts, execute them through ScriptRunner, and monitor progress in dedicated tabs. Depends on the Blender MCP integration and exposes FBX outputs consumed by the UE5 import flow.
contexts.name: blender-pipeline

contexts.description: Blueprint transpilation suite that parses UE5 Blueprint JSON exports into a semantic AST, diffs them structurally, and generates equivalent C++ with a Shiki-highlighted code viewer. A jargon/glossary system explains Blueprint nodes in plain language. Supports round-trip C++ → Blueprint import back into UE5 via the bridge.
contexts.name: blueprint-tools

contexts.description: Blueprint-to-C++ transpilation workbench plus top-level game-system configuration views (input, physics, save/load, multiplayer, dialogue). The transpiler takes pasted Blueprint JSON and produces header/source C++ via the useBlueprintTranspiler hook, with a diff pane and a write-to-project button that pushes files directly into the UE5 source tree. The game-system views provide module-level UI shells consumed by the module navigation layer.
contexts.name: blueprint-transpiler-game-systems

contexts.description: Tracks UE5 build history records per platform, exposes size-trend charts and build-comparison views, and manages build configuration profiles. Build records are persisted via the packaging build-history store (SQLite-backed API) and fetched with apiFetch; the dashboard tabs (history, trend, compare) visualize them using framer-motion and recharts. Depends on build-profiles library for platform normalization and projectStore for scope.
contexts.name: build-history-config

contexts.description: End-to-end UE5 build and packaging pipeline covering preflight checks, cook, smoke tests, and size-budget enforcement. A scheduled nightly build runs via the server-side cron in instrumentation.ts, skipping unchanged git HEADs. Exposes a multi-step wizard UI for manual build initiation and surfaces cook progress with phase segmentation.
contexts.name: build-packaging

contexts.description: Monitors UE5 build health by tracking cook targets, recurring errors, build duration trends, and batch module review status. BuildHealthDashboard shows per-target rows, regression banners, and error pattern tracking; PerformanceProfilingView imports CSV profiler data to surface frame-time and memory charts; BatchReviewPanel enables bulk CLI-driven review across multiple modules at once. All three read from build_runs and pipeline_artifacts tables.
contexts.name: build-quality-monitoring

contexts.description: Implements the full multi-tier acceptance verdict engine (L0–L4) used to grade every pipeline step's output. Provides composable checkers (graph structure, wiring contracts, UE static analysis, Python drain, link integrity, data shape, packaging) and the resolver that combines them with server-verdict overlays and LLM judge verdicts into a final `AcceptanceResult`. The `packaging/` subdirectory handles final UE5 artifact collection before the ship gate.
contexts.name: catalog-acceptance

contexts.description: The main LayoutLab interface serving as the application homepage: Category → Catalog → Entity tree with a Baseline entity-view panel for pipeline step navigation. A global coaching overlay (NextStepCoach, GlobalCoach) recommends the highest-value next action per entity. The LabBridgeStrip shows live UE5 connection status; responsive shell collapses to drawer panels below 1100px. Hydrates pipeline artifact state from the server on entity-open and renders a config-complete summary in the pipeline header. The Baseline module is now a directory with focused hooks (useEntityArtifacts, useStepJudgeVerdicts, useBatchDrain) and a roving-focus keyboard model.
contexts.name: catalog-browser-ui

contexts.description: Defines the shared types, step specification contract, pipeline registry, and supporting utilities that every catalog pipeline depends on. It establishes the `CatalogEntityBase` envelope and `LifecycleState` ladder, the `CatalogPipeline` / `StepSpec` authoring contract, and helpers for artifact validation, batch operations, UE schema bridging, table-view resolution, and headless pipeline execution. Everything else in `src/lib/catalog` imports from here.
contexts.name: catalog-core-infrastructure

contexts.description: SQLite persistence layer for catalog entities, pipeline artifacts (with revision history), and the canon authoritative data set. Exposes REST API routes for reading/writing pipeline artifacts, a drain endpoint that flips deferred L3/L4 artifacts to pass/fail after live UE5 verification, and revision routes for step history restore. The labArtifactClient on the frontend wraps these endpoints. Catalog seed helpers populate starter entities for every registered pipeline type on boot. Generated package manifests under generated/packages/ store the final UE-ready output for each entity.
contexts.name: catalog-database

contexts.description: Measures the distance between the current catalog state and the GDD target for every game-content domain, surfacing missing or incomplete entities as actionable gaps. The plugin architecture allows each catalog type (quests, audio, VFX, materials, characters, etc.) to define its own completeness criteria independently, with a shared plugin registry and index aggregating the results for the gap-loop campaign workflow.
contexts.name: catalog-gap-analysis

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/catalog, GET /api/catalog/entities, POST /api/catalog/lifecycle, GET /api/catalog/pipelines, GET /api/catalog/step-recipe, POST /api/catalog/step-submit, GET/POST /api/pipeline-artifacts, POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/drain, GET /api/pipeline-artifacts/drain/status, POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/drain/worker
contexts.description: Manages the full lifecycle of the catalog→UE content pipeline: entity registration, pipeline runs, step recipes, step submissions, and artifact drain/verification. Artifacts progress through a four-tier acceptance ladder (L0–L4) stored in pipeline_artifacts, with drain workers pushing accepted artifacts toward the UE project. Depends on the catalog-db and pipeline-db libraries; consumed by the pipeline step UI and harness.
contexts.name: catalog-pipeline-api

contexts.description: All domain models and state stores for the Catalog Pipeline lab: pipeline run state, artifact cache and client, catalog change tracking, content drift detection, acceptance logic, batch-drain model, glossary, and the Baseline entity view (which owns the per-entity, per-step work canvas). The Baseline subtree renders the step detail panel for a selected (catalog, entity) pair and is the primary data flow entry from shell to step components.
contexts.name: catalog-pipeline-state

contexts.description: Contains one self-registering pipeline definition per game-content catalog type, each declaring the ordered View/Produce/Acceptance steps, produce prompts, and checker wiring for its domain. Covers the full breadth of game content: characters, bestiary, items, loot tables, audio, music, VFX, materials, animations, combat map, zone map, state graph, screen flow, quests, factions, currencies, HUD elements, codex, and more. `registry.generated.ts` is the auto-generated index that `allCatalogPipelines()` reads.
contexts.name: catalog-pipelines

contexts.description: Provides the initial seeded game-world entities for every catalog type (spellbook abilities, items, loot tables, bestiary, characters, materials, audio, animation assets, zone map, state graph, screen flow, combat map) plus the canonical archetype definitions that enforce design-law constraints. The `canon/` subdirectory holds the archetype canon and its validation rules that govern how entities are judged across all pipeline steps. `new-catalogs.ts` wires later catalog additions into the section registry.
contexts.name: catalog-seed-data

contexts.description: Covers character movement design (dodge trajectory, state machine visualization, movement tab) and the AI-feel tuning panel (parameter presets, feel layer stack, comparison panel) plus a curve-editor playground with canvas-drawn acceleration/deceleration curves. Together these let designers tune character movement feel without leaving the browser. Depends on shared character data and the combat dodge-math utilities.
contexts.name: character-movement-playground

contexts.description: Covers the ARPG character module's overview, input-bindings, and features surfaces: property inspector, class hierarchy, hitbox wireframe viewer, scaling preview, camera-profile comparison, input binding visualizer (keyboard + mouse widget), character source wizard, and blueprint/movement metrics. This is the first panel a designer opens when inspecting a character archetype. Reads character data from the module store.
contexts.name: character-overview-input

contexts.description: Provides two balance-simulation panels for the ARPG character: a feedback-based simulator (stat inputs, config panel, metrics, results) and a predictive simulator (DPS breakdown, sensitivity charts, survival heatmap/curve, enemy sources, canon-checks). Also includes an archetype balance radar and cross-archetype comparison matrix. These tools let designers validate stat balance without leaving the browser.
contexts.name: character-simulator

contexts.description: Renders and interacts with the streamed output from a Claude CLI session inside the terminal shell. Transforms raw LogEntry and ToolUse events into formatted rows (ToolRows), extracts entity tags for quick navigation (EntityTags), and exposes a selection toolbar for copying or acting on text spans. useTerminalOutput drives the scroll-aware virtualized list and manages the display state for tool calls, file changes, and assistant messages.
contexts.name: cli-terminal-output

contexts.api_surface: Consumes /api/cli/* SSE endpoints; exposes onTaskComplete callback with CallbackStatus
contexts.description: Provides the embedded Claude Code CLI terminal used throughout the app to dispatch AI-powered UE5 code-generation tasks. CompactTerminal and InlineTerminal are the primary host components; they manage a task queue (useTaskQueue), session lifecycle, skill-pack injection (skills.ts), UE5 build-log parsing (UE5BuildParser), and dispatch-health monitoring so developers can run, track, and recover CLI sessions without leaving the browser. Depends on the CLI service layer in src/lib/claude-terminal and Zustand stores for panel state.
contexts.name: cli-terminal-shell

contexts.description: Claude Code CLI integration that spawns a CLI subprocess, parses stream-JSON output with session management, and wires domain-specific skills knowledge packs. The task system uses @@CALLBACK markers so Claude's output is intercepted, validated as JSON, and POSTed back to the app's API. The useModuleCLI hook is the standard way for module components to launch and track CLI sessions.
contexts.name: cli-terminal-system

contexts.description: AI-driven coaching surfaces that guide developers toward the next best action in the pipeline. GlobalCoach derives coach ladder recommendations from step acceptance verdicts; NextStepCoach renders the actionable prompt; DriftBanner and ProduceErrorBanner surface staleness and produce failures. RefreshFromServer and RefreshCatalogFromServer handle server-truth reconciliation triggers after external changes.
contexts.name: coach-and-guidance

contexts.description: Houses the deep multi-pass evaluation results viewer, judge-verdict browser, pattern library, and asset-code oracle for auditing generated UE5 C++ quality. DeepEvalResults shows per-module findings across the 4-pass eval (ground-truth → structure → quality → performance) with a progress panel; JudgeVerdictsView renders score trends and verdict detail modals; PatternLibraryView lets developers author and browse reusable code patterns; AssetCodeOracleView exposes consistency scores, dependency explorer, and violation rows for generated assets.
contexts.name: code-quality-evaluation

contexts.description: Handles the high-level combat choreography and flow: a unified pacing timeline with tension arc, spatial grid, swim-lane diagrams, combo chain diagram, and sequence diagrams. Also covers attribute defaults export and the combat module root navigation. Designers use these tools to review and tune the dramatic tension arc of an encounter over time.
contexts.name: combat-choreography

contexts.description: Models the full damage calculation pipeline as an interactive visual flow: damage nodes, formula steps, attribute phases, heal pipeline, direct health flow, and execution breakdown panel. Also covers combo ability sequencing (cooldown overlap chart, timeline blocks) and the hits tab plus combat-feel polish export. Outputs UE5-compatible execution snippets and combat-feel parameter files.
contexts.name: combat-damage-pipeline

contexts.description: Dedicated dodge-chain and frame-data tooling: a scrubbing dodge-chain timeline with playback controls, phase legend, velocity curve, hit-marker editor, rating badge, and live stats panel. Supports side-by-side chain parameter editing and exports frame data tables. Used by combat designers to precisely tune invincibility windows, recovery frames, and chain timing.
contexts.name: combat-dodge-timeline

contexts.description: Aggregated combat analytics dashboard: DPS metric, effectiveness, sankey diagram, cumulative damage SVG, grouped DPS bar chart, KPI metrics, stat influence panel, sequences and traces metrics. Backed by shared combat data and dodge-math utilities. Provides the quantitative read-out that balances against the qualitative choreography tools.
contexts.name: combat-metrics

contexts.description: Simulates ARPG combat encounters in-browser to validate balance and tuning parameters before integration into UE5. The view lets designers configure scenarios, tune sliders for damage/cooldown/threat, and inspect results via ability heatmaps, distribution charts, and fight-report cards. Results feed back into the combat balance pipeline and cross-reference the economy simulator for gear-economy interactions.
contexts.name: combat-simulator

contexts.description: Monitors and controls the UE5 cook and packaging pipeline: real-time cook progress logs, nightly build scheduling, preflight gate checks, and cook settings configuration. The useCookProgress hook polls the cook API and parses log rows; GateNotifySettings persists gate notification preferences; NightlyBuildScheduler configures scheduled headless builds. Feeds into the build history tracking context.
contexts.name: cook-packaging-pipeline

contexts.description: Shared cross-module tab infrastructure used by core-engine submodules: feature map initialization, genome build-code export and import, comparison matrix, accelerator/donut/dodge trajectory charts, and reusable tab navigation primitives. Acts as the design-system layer for all unique-tab extensions in the module. Depended on by all sub-module tab roots.
contexts.name: core-engine-genre-tabs

contexts.description: Provides the top-level module shell for game-design planning workflows: genre template gallery, DNA timeline, roadmap checklist, plan view, planning glossary, implementation plan tracker, and an interactive 2-D plan matrix map with canvas-based clusters and sectors. Developers open this context first when exploring module-level structure. Depends on Zustand module/project stores and the event bus for plan state.
contexts.name: core-engine-planning-shell

contexts.description: Provides code-scan finding review (ScanTab: list findings, resolve issues, hook to scan hook) and telemetry evolution analysis (TelemetryEvolution: accepted genres, pattern lists, scan history, suggestions). These tools surface static-analysis results and live telemetry signals to help developers track quality over time. Reads scan results from the module store and telemetry data via API.
contexts.name: core-engine-scan-telemetry

contexts.description: Crash report ingestion and analysis engine that parses UE5 crash logs, maps call stacks to known patterns via a glossary, and suggests fixes. The bridge-doctor component diagnoses live connection failures between the app and UE5. Integrates with the game director to surface crash regressions across sessions.
contexts.name: crash-analysis

contexts.description: Ingests UE5 crash logs and callstacks, runs AI diagnosis, and organises findings by pattern and severity so developers can triage regressions quickly. CrashAnalyzerView provides list/detail views with AI-generated diagnosis cards, plain-language summaries, and raw log display; CrashTimeMachine adds a frame-by-frame transport scrubber for replaying crash context over time. Both connect to the pof-mcp crash-analyze tool and the crash_records database table.
contexts.name: crash-analysis

contexts.description: Surfaces feature completion state across all game-dev modules in a single heatmap dashboard and provides the top-level EvaluatorModule shell that routes between all evaluator sub-views via a tab strip. CrossModuleFeatureDashboard renders heatmaps, overall summaries, and bottom panels for each module's feature status; EvaluatorModule is the root component for the entire evaluator section. Supporting primitives (EvaluatorCoachmark, ParamCue, ErrorMemoryPanel) are shared across sub-views.
contexts.name: cross-module-features

contexts.description: Single SQLite instance at ~/.pof/pof.db shared across all subsystems via better-sqlite3 in WAL mode. The db.ts module manages the connection lifecycle, migrations, and shared utilities. Each feature domain has its own *-db.ts file with typed query functions. next.config.ts externalizes better-sqlite3 to prevent bundling on the server.
contexts.name: database-layer

contexts.description: Runtime debug dashboard for the game module: crash prediction, regression section, stat dashboard, network section, draw-call profiler, GC timeline, memory section, system health gauge (circular gauge), and a command catalog console. Shared data fixtures back the mock panels. Used by developers to triage performance and crash signals without leaving the PoF app.
contexts.name: debug-performance

contexts.description: Models and validates the in-game loot economy by simulating gold flow, wealth distribution, supply-demand curves, and goal-seek targets. The view exposes a configuration panel and a tornado sensitivity section so designers can tune faucet/sink parameters, then generates UE5-ready data table code via EconomyCodeGenPanel. Integrates with the economy catalog API and surfaces a run-history strip for comparing simulation iterations.
contexts.name: economy-simulator

contexts.description: Visual design tools for spatial combat authoring: EQS component inventory and pipeline diagrams, squad formation choreography with code-gen, attack-ring visualizers, and patrol-point distribution charts. Designers configure UE5 Environment Query System pipelines and squad tactics interactively, then export generated Blueprint or C++ scaffolding. Consumes EQS catalog data and feeds into the blueprint transpiler context.
contexts.name: eqs-squad-combat-spatial

contexts.description: Hooks that manage the feature matrix, game design documents, and design-state derived views used across all module panels. They fetch and mutate feature rows, compute visibility and init-status guards, surface genre-evolution trajectories, and bridge activity-feed events between the editor and the pipeline. Entity commit buffers and track-help hooks coordinate staged writes back to the DB without losing intermediate state.
contexts.name: feature-design-state-hooks

contexts.description: Tracks the implementation status of every game feature across all modules in a visual matrix view, powered by a SQLite backing store. The Feature Constellation renders a layered tech-tree dependency graph for a single module with status-colored nodes and a recommended-next pulse. The NBA engine reads these statuses to suggest the highest-value next action.
contexts.name: feature-matrix-tracking

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/ability-spec, POST /api/ability-spec/codegen, GET/POST /api/feature-matrix, GET /api/feature-matrix/all-statuses, GET /api/feature-matrix/progress, POST /api/game-design-doc, POST /api/gdd-compliance, POST /api/quest-generation, POST /api/combat-simulator, POST /api/economy-simulator, POST /api/economy-simulator/goal-seek, POST /api/economy-simulator/sweep, POST /api/localization-pipeline
contexts.description: Exposes the game design authoring APIs: ability spec CRUD and code generation, feature-matrix status and history tracking (NBA engine backbone), GDD document management and compliance scoring, quest generation, game director session tracking, balance baseline snapshots, combat and economy simulation (including goal-seek and parameter sweep), and localization pipeline. Covers the full design→balance→ship loop from spec to verified UE data.
contexts.name: game-design-studio-api

contexts.description: Session-level project health tracking that aggregates build quality scores, regression signals, and crash trends across development sessions. The severity legend surfaces critical findings with one-click fix suggestions and a regression tracker diffs session vs session. The dzin (src/lib/dzin/) and ecw (src/lib/ecw/) modules provide entity-level roadmap summaries, milestone forecasts, progress tracks, and shell preferences for a longer-horizon planning view that complements the session-scoped game-director data.
contexts.name: game-director-system

contexts.description: UMG/UE5 HUD and widget authoring module: accessibility tab, flow graph with screen-node rows, HUD compositor (widget summary, rect layout, composer index), ARPG HUD preview, systems tab, UI bindings tab, and a WBP starter panel with widget class definitions. Lets designers lay out and audit the in-game HUD widget hierarchy before writing UMG C++ code.
contexts.name: game-ui-hud

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/audio-gen, POST /api/audio-scene, POST /api/spatial-audio-generate, GET/POST /api/animation-ledger, POST /api/animations/mixamo-result, GET/POST /api/level-design, POST /api/level-design/procgen-result, POST /api/procgen/zone-pins, POST /api/post-process-studio
contexts.description: API layer for game-world content creation: audio generation (ElevenLabs TTS, spatial audio, scene mixing, codegen), animation ledger and Mixamo result ingestion, pattern library management, level-design operations (procgen, scatter, sync with UE), procedural zone-pin generation, and post-process studio parameter tuning. Connects the creative UI to provider APIs and the UE project.
contexts.name: game-world-content-api

contexts.description: Game Design Document tooling that validates implementation against a structured GDD, synthesizes design documents from game metadata, and renders the GDD as an interactive Mermaid architecture diagram with clickable nodes that jump to the relevant module. The GDD pitch tool generates investor/producer-ready summaries. Depends on module navigation to wire diagram clicks to the workspace.
contexts.name: gdd-compliance

contexts.description: Checks implementation completeness against the Game Design Document by mapping features to GDD sections, surfacing gaps, and showing evidence strips. GDDComplianceView renders module cards with gap indicators, suggestion panels, and mapping strips; GameDesignDocView provides markdown-rendered GDD section browsing; CodebaseArcheologistView analyses churn, anti-patterns, and backlog debt trends. Together they close the loop between the written design and shipped code.
contexts.name: gdd-compliance

contexts.description: Autonomous development harness that orchestrates multi-step game feature builds end-to-end: authoring spec, generating C++, submitting to UE5 via the bridge, running tests, and verifying via visual capture. The pof-mcp stdio server exposes harness capabilities to Claude Code CLI as MCP tools, enabling fully autonomous iteration loops from the terminal.
contexts.name: harness-autonomy

contexts.description: Delivers a multi-tab holistic view of project quality across velocity, milestone, and quality dimensions alongside a unified summary that consolidates signals from all evaluator sub-views. HolisticHealthView renders milestone tracking, performance stat cards, and quality heatmaps; UnifiedSummaryView aggregates dimension bars, health gauges, and quick-nav cards into a single entry point. Both use custom hooks to fetch and normalise data from multiple API endpoints.
contexts.name: holistic-quality-overview

contexts.description: Covers three HUD design subsystems: DamageNumberPhysicsSimulator provides a canvas-based physics sandbox for tuning floating combat text trajectories, arc, and clutter; MenuFlowDiagram is a node-graph editor for designing screen-to-screen menu navigation flows with transition arrows; LowHealthPulse is a parameterised pulse animation tool for the low-health screen effect. Shared standalone components (DamageNumberPalette, EnemyHealthBarFSM, UIHudView) round out the module's HUD authoring surface.
contexts.name: hud-damage-and-navigation

contexts.description: Two HUD/UI design tools: HudThemeEditor lets designers author and live-preview in-game HUD theme parameters (colours, fade timelines, animation curves) with CSS variable exports; InventoryGridDesigner provides an interactive grid layout designer for inventory/equipment screens, allowing designers to configure slot dimensions, slot types, equip zones, and interaction behaviors. Both tools export their configurations as UE5-ready data.
contexts.name: hud-theme-and-inventory

contexts.description: AI 2D image generation pipeline supporting Leonardo.ai (tiling, transparency, ControlNet, upscaler) and Qwen VLM (image recognition/critique). Every generation downloads then deletes the asset from the provider. Style DNA captures per-project art direction (style-dna.ts, style-dna-db.ts) and is injected into prompt chips. The one-shot lab enables rapid single-image generation; best-of-n runs parallel generations and auto-selects the highest quality. A generated-icons system (generated-icons.ts) serves per-step icon assets to gallery steps via /api/visual-gen/icons. The asset library (asset-library-db.ts, library-filter.ts) tracks all downloaded assets with license metadata.
contexts.name: image-generation

contexts.description: Gear catalog browser for the inventory module: item grid, detail drawer, comparison panel, affix slot panels, sunburst chart, set bonus section, equipment loadout, catalog filters, trading card with tooltip, and a spatial stash grid (drag-and-drop 2-D inventory layout). This is the primary gear-browsing surface for designers reviewing item power across the catalog.
contexts.name: inventory-catalog

contexts.description: Inventory economy simulation and loot-filter rule builder: an affix-alert economy simulator with power-curve charts, rarity stack charts, alert cards, heatmap, and simulation results; plus a drag-and-drop loot-filter rule builder with live preview, export panel, rule list, and ruleset toolbar. Designers use these to validate economy health at scale and author player-facing loot filter scripts.
contexts.name: inventory-economy-simulator

contexts.description: Item DNA genome editor and economy sourcing: genome strand editor (trait sliders, distribution bars, code preview, Monte Carlo roller), breeding/evolution/library tabs, genome selector, and economy sourcing (crafting recipes, drop sources, sankey diagram, item scaling chart, rarity distribution). Together these surfaces let designers encode item identity as a genome and trace where items come from economically.
contexts.name: inventory-genome-economy

contexts.description: The reference implementation of the catalog pipeline for the Items catalog (15 steps including economy, art, attributes, concept-brief, anim-audio, integration, etc.). Serves as the canonical example of how every catalog pipeline should be built using CliProduce + StepFrame + CandidateGallery. Tests serve as the regression guard for the pipeline authoring conventions. The items pipeline is exercised by the dedicated e2e spec while all other catalogs are covered by the generic walker.
contexts.name: item-catalog-pipeline

contexts.description: AAA-lens quality scoring engine operating on two axes: the judge fleet (rubrics-based multi-dimensional scoring with content hashing, sibling context awareness, spend metering, and verdict trend tracking) and the craft loop (per-cell lens verdicts from 10 authored AAA rubric lenses in lib/craft/lenses/). Judge verdicts are stored in judge_verdicts and exposed via REST; craft verdicts in craft_verdicts. The status dashboard reads both to produce the A-axis quality layer beside the R-ladder. verdictStanding aggregates per-step judge outputs into a single PASS/FAIL/VERIFIED signal; fleetPlan orchestrates which rubric dimensions to evaluate per payload type.
contexts.name: judge-craft-quality

contexts.description: Domain knowledge base that powers the skills system injected into CLI sessions. Contains structured knowledge about UE5 assets, gotchas, patterns, and best practices. The implementation planner uses this knowledge to generate step-by-step build plans. The localization system provides i18n knowledge for UE5 content pipelines.
contexts.name: knowledge-system

contexts.description: React hooks adapter layer for the Catalog Pipeline lab — bridges domain state stores to component props. Covers catalog refresh, entity artifact loading, batch drain execution, lab activity tracking, user preferences, last-visit state, roving keyboard focus, and step judge verdict queries.
contexts.name: lab-hooks

contexts.description: The outer LayoutLab shell that renders the /layout route — full-screen composer with catalog selector, entity list, pipeline timeline rail, drawer navigation, UE bridge status strip, and crash containment. It owns the theme/font tokens, the matrix loading skeleton, the batch-drain bind UI, and search shortcut. Entry points route the user between catalog entities and pass the selected step position down as a single source of truth to avoid remount drift.
contexts.name: lab-shell-and-navigation

contexts.description: Lab-scoped design-token-aware UI atom library: Button, IconButton, Chip, Field, Panel, Rail, Stat, Skeleton, SearchCombobox, and VisuallyHidden. These are intentionally scoped to the lab rather than the global ui/ directory because they use lab-specific CSS tokens (lab-tokens.css) and the lab's own theming contract. Consumed exclusively within the layout-lab subtree.
contexts.name: lab-ui-primitives

contexts.description: Procedural level generation tools that let designers describe a world in plain language and receive a scatter/placement plan. Supports zone graph generation, PCG (Procedural Content Generation) integration, and a live in-browser procgen preview. The text-to-world flow converts narrative descriptions into actionable UE5 PCG parameters.
contexts.name: level-design-module

contexts.description: Provides the level design document viewer and a node-graph flow editor for room/area connectivity. LevelDesignView is the top-level shell with tabbed document navigation, a sync indicator, and a commit buffer for debounced saves; LevelFlowEditor renders a drag-and-drop canvas of room nodes connected by transition lines; LevelDesignSpatialDiagram renders a spatial minimap of area relationships. Together they give designers a living, editable document workspace linked to UE5 level streaming state.
contexts.name: level-flow-editor

contexts.description: Manages and QA-reviews the UE5 localization pipeline end-to-end: string extraction, translation review, expansion-factor analysis, and hazard detection for layout-breaking strings. The view organises across Overview, Strings, Translations, and QA subtabs; useLocalizationPipelineView drives data fetching and state; supporting cards handle string tables, translation pairs, QA findings, replacement candidates, and readiness-to-ship gating. Reads from localization_strings and translation_jobs tables.
contexts.name: localization-pipeline

contexts.description: Core loot module structure and affix tooling: the loot module root/nav, loot-table editor (import, paginate, search/filter, re-export), affix roll simulator, core loot utilities (enemy binding, EV calculator, weight distribution, world item preview), and shared loot math/codegen/design primitives. This is the entry context for the entire loot sub-module.
contexts.name: loot-affix-core

contexts.description: Interactive affix crafting workbench for item creation and balancing: crafting station, affix pool panel, item base selector, item preview card, breakpoint table with filters/legend/rows, crafting log, item stats summary, and a full codegen pipeline (exports UE5-ready affix data tables). Designers craft gear here to verify power budget and affix synergies.
contexts.name: loot-affix-workbench

contexts.description: Loot analytics dashboard and AI-assisted loot designer: metrics for beacon, co-occurrence, drought, histogram, impact, pipeline, simulator, timer, treemap, weights, and world items. Also includes an AI loot designer with distribution panel, co-occurrence panel, metrics/weights view, and code panel. Provides the read-out layer over simulation results and an LLM-backed design pathway.
contexts.name: loot-metrics-designer

contexts.description: Monte-Carlo loot drop simulation and economy analysis: drop simulator, drops-per-hour chart, treemap, histogram, loot diff section, pity timer (drought calculator + pity timer section), and loot economy (beacon visualizer, economy filters, impact table, economy summary grid, smart loot). Lets designers stress-test drop rates and economy health at scale.
contexts.name: loot-simulation

contexts.description: The primary materials module surface — a tabbed view (Ask, Configurator, Hierarchy, Patterns, PostProcess, StyleTransfer) for configuring UE5 material parameters, browsing pattern catalogs, and managing material layer hierarchies. MaterialParameterConfigurator renders parameter sections with live sliders and pickers; MaterialPatternCatalog cards let designers select and apply named tiling patterns; shared display utilities MaterialBudgetBar and MaterialLayerGraph show shader cost and layer structure. The MaterialsView root composes all tabs.
contexts.name: material-configurator

contexts.api_surface: Calls UE5 Remote Control API for material application; reads /api/visual-gen/material endpoints
contexts.description: PBR material authoring and preview environment where designers configure tiling textures, run the Advanced Texture Panel pipeline, and export materials to UE5. Provides a real-time MaterialPreview, a PBR parameter editor, material transfer utilities, and a UE5 export panel. Backed by useMaterialStore (Zustand) and calls UE5 Remote Control to apply materials in-engine.
contexts.name: material-lab

contexts.description: Provides two advanced material authoring tools: MaterialStyleTransfer analyzes a reference image or texture and transfers its stylistic properties (colour, roughness, metalness adjustments) onto a target material via a multi-step analysis flow with mini-previews; PostProcessStackBuilder lets designers compose and order a stack of post-process effects with per-effect sliders. Both tools bridge art-direction intent to exportable UE5 material/PP parameter sets.
contexts.name: material-style-tools

contexts.description: Tracks the inventory of 3D model assets bridged between the PoF pipeline and UE5 — showing asset cards, bridge manifest entries, a dependency graph, and filter chips for asset type/status. AssetInventory renders a filterable card grid sourced from pipeline_artifacts and the bridge manifest; AssetPipelineDiagram visualises the generative pipeline stages each asset has passed through; ModelsView is the top-level shell composing these panels.
contexts.name: models-asset-inventory

contexts.description: Hooks that drive the CLI terminal sessions for each game-design module — launching checklist tasks, dispatching reviews, tracking spend, and computing Next Best Action recommendations. They compose TaskFactory prompts, gate expensive calls through the preflight spend system, and record outcomes into session analytics. The NBA engine reads feature-status and run-evidence to rank what the developer should work on next.
contexts.name: module-cli-orchestration-hooks

contexts.description: Four-pass quality evaluation system (ground-truth → structure → quality → performance) that runs automated assessments against each module's code. Deep eval runs multi-dimensional scoring in parallel across configurable prompts. The evaluator module renders scorecards, trend charts, and drill-down views per evaluation pass. Results feed the Game Director's quality regression tracking and the judge-craft-quality engine reads evaluator verdicts to populate the craft_verdicts table for the A-axis quality layer in the status dashboard.
contexts.name: module-evaluator

contexts.description: Defines the core module registry that organizes the game development workspace into domain-specific modules (combat, animation, loot, etc.) each with checklists, quick actions, and knowledge tips. The registry drives what checklist items, prompts, and NBA (Next Best Action) recommendations appear in the UI. Depends on feature-definitions for the dependency graph that powers cross-module navigation.
contexts.name: module-system

contexts.description: Visualises the dependency graph between all game-dev modules and features so developers can understand coupling and plan changes safely. DependencyGraph renders a force-directed canvas graph with controls and legend; NexusView adds a deep-dive panel with pipeline-status nodes; FeatureConstellation plots features as a star-map with next-best-action callouts; CrossModuleOverlapPanel surfaces shared checklist items between modules. All views share the moduleTopology utility for graph layout.
contexts.name: module-topology-graph

contexts.description: Test gate runner that executes L3/L4 pipeline acceptance gates against the live UE5 editor via pluggable executors (bridge/spawn/visual). The drain API flips deferred artifacts to pass/fail after verification. The observation spine defines typed contracts for what can be measured (position, animation-state, health, damage, timing). Visual capture feeds frames to the VLM critique gate.
contexts.name: observation-testing

contexts.description: Acceptance logic engine that derives L0–L4 tier status (data/human-selection/static/runtime/visual) from pipeline artifact state rather than manual toggles. Resolves config-complete vs deferred status and provides the language/labels used in acceptance banners. The judgeBridge integrates judge-fleet verdicts into the acceptance resolution chain. bindGeneratedIcons and bindIconsAll wire produced icon assets into gallery acceptance. pythonDrain handles acceptance for Python-executed drain gates. The acceptance engine is the single source of truth for pipeline step completion.
contexts.name: pipeline-acceptance-engine

contexts.description: Individual pipeline step panel components for the Items catalog (ConceptBrief, Economy, Attributes, Art, AnimAudio, Gate, Integration) plus the generic ArchetypeStep that serves all ~330 non-Items steps across every catalog. Also includes the one-shot pipeline run flow (OneShotPanel, ProposalView, DistributionView, RunLogView, CatalogPickerForm) which lets a developer execute a full pipeline from a single prompt.
contexts.name: pipeline-step-components

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/checklist/complete, GET /api/checklist-metadata, POST /api/notify/gate, GET /api/cli-spend, GET/POST /api/cli-task-registry, POST /api/packaging/execute, GET /api/packaging/history, POST /api/packaging/preflight, GET/POST /api/packaging/profiles, POST /api/packaging/schedule, POST /api/packaging/smoke-test, GET /api/marketplace, POST /api/module-scan/import, POST /api/preview/hydrate, GET/POST /api/scenario
contexts.description: Core platform services that cut across modules: checklist completion callbacks (@@CALLBACK markers resolved here), gate notifications, CLI spend tracking, CLI task registry, packaging operations (preflight, execute, smoke-test, schedule, profiles, history), marketplace listing, module scan import, preview hydration and tuning, and scenario management. These are the plumbing routes that all module UIs depend on for shared operations.
contexts.name: platform-services-api

contexts.description: Wizard-driven procedural level generation — the designer picks a level type, algorithm, size parameters, and constraints, then generates a dungeon layout with live preview, spawn placement, and export to a Blender/UE5-compatible spec. Supporting panels include biome scatter, pacing/difficulty reporting, procgen dungeon preview and replay export, run history, and per-room detail. All generation runs are recorded for history replay and regression comparison.
contexts.name: procedural-level-generation

contexts.api_surface: Calls UE5 Remote Control for scene export; reads /api/visual-gen/procedural; triggers pof-mcp import pipeline
contexts.description: Grouped toolset covering procedural mesh generation, scene composition, character auto-rigging, and UE5 import automation. The ProceduralEngine lets artists tweak parameters and preview randomised geometry; SceneComposer manages a scene tree and exports to UE5; AutoRig applies preset rigs to imported meshes; ImportAutomation orchestrates the end-to-end ingest. These four lightweight modules share the visual-gen output path and are too small to stand alone.
contexts.name: procedural-scene-tools

contexts.description: XP curve design and build-path tooling: multi-curve overlay, XP curve chart with parameter panel, milestone timeline, curve delta summary, build path comparison, XP source breakdown, power-curve danger zones, diminishing-returns visualizer, and shared chart math. Designers use these to author and compare leveling curves and build paths before generating UE5 data tables.
contexts.name: progression-curves-builds

contexts.description: Reward authoring and progression internals: level-up reward preview, achievement board, rest-XP system, time-to-level estimator, prestige preview, and three code-generator tools (DR code generator, encounter TTK simulator, XP table generator) each with their own helpers and type definitions. These internals feed UE5 data tables for the live progression system.
contexts.name: progression-rewards-internals

contexts.api_surface: Bridge Blueprint inspection endpoints; filesystem path enumeration
contexts.description: Provides two lightweight inspection tools for navigating an existing UE5 project: PathBrowser lets the user browse and select filesystem paths relative to the UE5 project root, while BlueprintInspector fetches and renders Blueprint asset metadata (variables, functions, graph sections) via the bridge. Both are on-demand panels consumed by ProjectSetupModule for reference and troubleshooting after a project is detected.
contexts.name: project-exploration-tools

contexts.description: Provides per-module and aggregate quality score dashboards that track game development progress across all UE5 modules. ProjectHealthDashboard renders radar charts, regression alerts, and scan-history timelines while AggregateQualityDashboard shows cross-module heatmaps, sparklines, and stale-review panels. Both read from the evaluation scan store and the SQLite scan_results tables.
contexts.name: project-health-dashboards

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/project-health, GET /api/project-progress, GET/POST /api/project-rules, GET /api/recent-projects, GET /api/session-analytics, POST /api/session-log, POST /api/telemetry, GET/POST /api/error-memory, GET /api/milestone-deadlines, GET /api/weekly-digest, GET /api/workflow-dag, GET /api/search
contexts.description: Project-level observability and reporting: health checks, progress rollups, project rules management, session analytics and logs, telemetry ingestion, error memory (persists UE build errors for prompt injection), milestone deadlines, weekly digest generation, workflow DAG rendering, and global search. These routes power the project dashboard and the ambient health indicators throughout the UI.
contexts.name: project-ops-api

contexts.description: Guides the developer through the full UE5 project bootstrapping flow: locating or creating a project, verifying the build environment, installing missing tooling, and exporting a setup manifest. A useProjectScan hook drives a status checklist and a derived next-step engine (nextStep.ts) that surfaces the single most important action at any moment. Prompts for CLI-assisted project creation and build verification are authored here and dispatched via useModuleCLI.
contexts.name: project-setup-core

contexts.description: Composable prompt construction system that injects UE5 project context into AI prompts for each module checklist item. A fluent builder assembles prompts across six sections (Project Context → Domain Context → Task Instructions → Best Practices → Output Schema → Success Criteria), with per-module specializations and a prompt evolution system that tracks versions and diffs. Central to the entire app's value proposition of generating UE5-specific code guidance.
contexts.name: prompt-engineering

contexts.description: Provides a full lifecycle view for evolving and A/B testing AI prompts: variant authoring, cluster analysis, test-run panels, judge-fitness scoring, and a version timeline with diff comparison. PromptEvolutionView manages variant cards, optimizer suggestions, and A/B test cards backed by the prompt_variants and ab_tests tables; PromptVersionTimeline renders a branching history tree for any prompt with statistical badges per version. Drives the quality improvement loop for the 4-pass evaluation system.
contexts.name: prompt-evolution

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/evaluator/results, GET /api/evaluator/deltas, GET/POST /api/judge-verdicts, GET /api/judge-verdicts/history, POST /api/harness, GET /api/harness/runs, GET /api/harness/runs/[id], POST /api/crash-analyzer, GET /api/regression-tracker, POST /api/verify/animation, POST /api/verify/visual, POST /api/experiment/run, GET /api/experiment/status/[id]
contexts.description: Drives the quality and regression system: multi-pass LLM evaluator results and deltas, judge verdict storage with history, craft verdicts, the autonomous harness (run management, screenshots, diffs), crash analysis, regression tracking, animation and visual verification endpoints, and UE experiment runs with status polling. Together these routes form the quality gate that gates pipeline artifacts and harness builds.
contexts.name: quality-evaluation-api

contexts.description: Manages project planning and AI workflow orchestration: CalendarRoadmapView renders a Gantt timeline with milestone cards, roadmap legend, and a custom hook for scheduling data; WorkflowOrchestratorView lets designers select module targets, browse execution templates, monitor active workflows, and review execution history. Together they support sprint planning and supervised multi-agent pipeline execution. Both depend on the milestones and workflow_runs tables.
contexts.name: roadmap-workflow-management

contexts.description: USaveGame schema design and management tooling: schema tree browser, save diff viewer, memory banks, file-size breakdown, budget alerting, slot management, integrity validator, version history with migration path graph, serialization profiler, auto-save config, cloud sync status, and data recovery tool. Helps developers design and audit UE5 save-game schemas before writing C++ serialization code.
contexts.name: save-system

contexts.description: Tracks developer session activity, token spend, and quality-score trends to give an ongoing view of AI-assisted development productivity. SessionAnalyticsDashboard and WeeklyDigestView surface module leaderboards, daily activity bars, and quality-score rows; SpendDashboard/SpendBudgetPanel monitor token cost; ProjectWrappedView generates shareable summary cards exported as canvas posters or markdown. Reads from the sessions and spend tables via REST.
contexts.name: session-analytics-reporting

contexts.description: General-purpose React hooks shared across all features: lifecycle management with guaranteed init/dispose semantics, suspend/LRU freeze integration, generic CRUD data-fetching with loading/error state, and low-level browser primitives (viewport, element size, pointer type, scroll restoration, keyboard shortcuts). They have no domain knowledge and no direct store dependencies — every feature module imports from this pool to avoid reinventing common React patterns.
contexts.name: shared-utility-hooks

contexts.description: Interactive combat and economy simulation environments that let designers validate balance without running UE5. The combat simulator models damage pipelines, dodge chains, and hit reactions with real-time parameter tuning. The economy simulator runs sensitivity sweeps on loot distribution and faucet/sink tables. Both export validated configs back to the catalog pipeline.
contexts.name: simulation-tools

contexts.description: 37 Zustand stores with persist middleware providing centralized state for every feature domain. Transient runtime fields are excluded from persistence to prevent snapshot instability on rehydration. The ProjectModuleBridge service breaks the circular dependency between project and module stores. The event bus provides typed pub/sub with a replay buffer for cross-store communication.
contexts.name: state-management

contexts.description: Project-wide status health map at /status showing pipeline coverage per catalog with tier stripes (L0–L4), capability model benchmarks, item-focus detail views, and model performance comparisons. The statusModel derives engine attribution (verified/trusted/ungated/dark) from step-facts.json and judge-verdicts; readiness.ts computes a readiness score across pipeline completeness, UE test gates, and craft-loop ceilings. Each pipeline swimlane is clickable, surfacing evidence modals with audit provenance. The Dev Inspector (_dev-inspector) provides a developer-facing overlay for locating components and inspecting capability coverage.
contexts.name: status-health-dashboard

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/visual-gen/icons, GET /api/visual-gen/assets, GET /api/visual-gen/icon/<name>, GET /api/visual-gen/asset/<name>, GET /api/cli-spend, GET /api/pipeline-artifacts/revisions, POST /api/pipeline-artifacts/revisions
contexts.description: Reusable building blocks consumed by every pipeline step: CandidateGallery (generative selection with bounded history), GlbViewer/GlbPreviewPanel (interactive 3D mesh preview), CliProduce (the standardised Produce panel with direction textarea and prompt logic), DataTable, ChartPanel, ProvenanceStrip (honesty disclosures on acceptance verdicts), StepHistoryPanel, StepLibraryPicker, and acceptance hooks (useStepAcceptance, useGenerativeStep). Also includes all candidate-generator utilities, asset-fetch hooks, and fix-copy for the archetype banners.
contexts.name: step-shared-primitives

contexts.description: A grid-based painter tool for designing UE5 World Partition streaming zones and their transition rules. Designers paint zones onto a grid, configure each zone's properties via ZoneEditor, and define streaming transitions between adjacent zones in a TransitionList. The planner maintains zone state in a custom hook and renders transition overlay lines on the grid canvas for visual clarity.
contexts.name: streaming-zone-planner

contexts.business_feature: Top Bar, Activity Feed & Global Search
contexts.description: Delivers the application top bar (project switcher, build-bridge indicator, notification badge, project stats, header actions) alongside the global search panel and the activity feed panel. The activity feed renders event-bus events as grouped, collapsible cards; GlobalSearchPanel queries modules and features in real time; EventBusDevTools provides a debug overlay for inspecting live pub/sub traffic.
contexts.name: topbar-and-activity

contexts.description: Hooks that bridge the browser to the UE5 engine and the asset-generation pipeline: they manage the SSE-backed Remote Control connection, source-sync round-trips, catalog generation steps, Blueprint-to-C++ transpilation, AI testing runs, and the canvas/scrub/audio preview surfaces for generated assets. PofBridge hooks coordinate verification-engine calls and write results back to the feature matrix. Collection editor, snapshot, and drag/angle hooks support the visual review UI for in-progress assets.
contexts.name: ue5-asset-generation-hooks

contexts.description: Dual-bridge communication layer to UE5: the mcp-unreal bridge (port 8090) for general editor commands and the PoF Bridge plugin (port 30040) for game-specific automation including run-automation, snapshot capture, and manifest queries. The pofBridgeStore tracks connection health; the ue5BridgeStore tracks build/compile status. Used by every subsystem that needs to verify state in the running UE5 editor.
contexts.name: ue5-bridge-client

contexts.api_surface: Bridge health polling endpoints; test harness scenario execution API
contexts.description: Monitors the health of all UE5 bridge subsystem endpoints (latency sparklines, connection settings, per-subsystem status) and provides a test-harness panel for running, browsing, and snapshotting UE5 integration scenarios. BridgeEndpointHealth polls bridge endpoints and renders latency history; TestHarnessPanel organises test suites, scenario cards, and result/snapshot tabs. Both panels share a pattern of a custom hook owning async state, constants defining endpoint slugs and defaults, and helper functions for formatting.
contexts.name: ue5-bridge-monitoring

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/ue5-bridge/build, GET /api/ue5-bridge/build-health, GET /api/ue5-bridge/status, POST /api/pof-bridge/compile, POST /api/pof-bridge/compile/hot-patch, GET /api/pof-bridge/manifest, POST /api/blueprint-transpiler, POST /api/ue5-inject-item, GET /api/ue5-source/parse
contexts.description: Bidirectional bridge between the PoF app and the UE5 project: triggers C++ compilation (including hot-patch), queries build health and status, reads the UE source manifest and blueprint definitions, and injects items into the UE data tables. Also hosts the Blueprint transpiler (generates C++ GAS code from Blueprint descriptions) and scaffolds UE functional tests.
contexts.name: ue5-build-bridge

contexts.description: Scenario harness for running controlled experiments in UE5: authoring scenario JSON, submitting to the PoF Bridge's inbox, reading captured observation frames, and comparing results across configurations. The Observation Spine (SP1) defines five observation verbs (position, animation state, health, etc.) with typed contracts verified by 21 tests. The reality ledger reconciles referenced vs existing vs valid vs runtime assets.
contexts.name: ue5-experiment-runner

The output meshes feed downstream mesh-quality and rigging pipelines.

contexts.description: Enforces geometry budget, UV quality, and aesthetic acceptance before a mesh is allowed through the production pipeline. Implements polycount presets, texel-density and world-scale validation, seam detection, scene cropping, and a multi-pass critique/best-of-N selector. Gate modules (input-gate, footage-gate, sheet-gate, view-gate) act as pass/fail checkpoints backed by async job stores.

contexts.description: Quality-gating scripts for generated meshes and animations, plus the ARDY motion-data pipeline.
